angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 30,701,241 km at 40.15 pc = 10.22 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 131873: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 24.91 +/- 0.12 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ac2431): 40.145 +/- 0.193 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 44.13 +/- 0.22 solar radii from Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 131873: radius 44.13 +/- 0.22 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 10.229 +/- 0.012 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ac2431): 30,701,241 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.3 +/- 0.3 solar masses from Tarrant et al. (2008), A&A 483, L43, abstract: 1.3 +/- 0.3 solar masses from the large frequency spacing, 0.48 microhertz, of two oscillation modes in SMEI photometry, with the star's known parameters (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361:200809738); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4008 +/- 37 K from Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 131873: effective temperature 4008 +/- 37 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ac2431). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Baines et al. (2021), AJ 162, 198, HD 131873: effective temperature 4008 +/- 37 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-3881/ac2431)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/kochab.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 1.263, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (HST/STIS Next Generation Spectral Library v2 (Heap & Lindler; MAST high-level science product), HD 131873) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
